bug.title: Kline parsing assumes milliseconds, so every Binance archive file from 2025 on overflows (microsecond timestamps)
bug.symptoms: nullius_ingest.klines._parse_candle passes open_time and close_time through _as_epoch_millis and _millis_to_utc. Binance's archive CSVs from 2025-01 on carry 16-digit microsecond epochs (1735689600000000 for 2025-01-01T00:00Z), so _millis_to_utc raises OverflowError, and the survivorship-free backfill dies on the first 2025 file it reads.
bug.reproduction_steps: Parse the first CSV row of the pinned BTCUSDT-1d-2025-01.zip with parse_klines: OverflowError.
bug.expected: - Epoch values are read by magnitude: - 13 digits (or below 10^14) is milliseconds - 16 digits (10^15 to 10^17) is microseconds and is converted exactly to the same instant - any other magnitude is refused with a named error. It is never guessed and never overflows. The live REST path, which is milliseconds, is unchanged. - The 2024-12 and 2025-01 pinned files both parse to UTC midnight open times: 2024-12-01T00:00Z and 2025-01-01T00:00Z respectively. - close_time is handled the same way. - test_archive_timestamp_units.py covers both pinned zips (checksums verified first), a mixed-unit sequence across a year boundary, a refused 19-digit value, and the REST fixtures' millisecond rows unchanged. It passes under pytest-xdist.
bug.actual: Root cause: klines treats every epoch as milliseconds; Binance's archive changed spot timestamps to microseconds from 2025.
bug.constraints: No file outside the two listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/

bug.title: The archive backfill shows no progress, keeps nothing until the very end, and dies with a raw traceback, so a multi-hour run that fails loses everything
bug.symptoms: `./run.sh lake-backfill --source archive --top 100` over 2019-2026: - It printed nothing for 2h20m. It ranks every USDT symbol over the whole window before writing any partition: about 565 MiB of archive listings and files were read at about 8 MiB/min with no output. - It then died on bug 1 with a Python traceback, not a one-line refusal. - It left no Parquet partitions and no ranking cache, so a rerun starts from zero.
bug.reproduction_steps: Run the archive backfill over a multi-year window; stop it or let it fail partway: no output during ranking, nothing persisted, and a traceback on failure.
bug.expected: - Progress: one JSON line per ranked symbol batch during ranking ({"phase": "rank", "symbols_done": n, "symbols_total": m}), then the existing per-symbol lines. - Checkpoint and resume: - The ranking result is cached in <LAKE>/staging-meta/rank-<window>.json once computed. - Each monthly archive file is verified and written into its bars partitions as it is fetched, not at the end. - A rerun with the same arguments reuses the cache, skips months already written (checked by partition presence), and finishes from where it stopped. - --restart ignores both and starts clean. The cache sits outside staging/ so it is never sealed. - Failure handling: any per-file failure (checksum mismatch, unparseable row) is one JSON error line naming symbol and month, and that month is skipped. The command exits 1 at the end if any month failed, with a summary line. An unexpected error exits 1 with one stderr line and no traceback. - test_backfill_resume_progress.py, with an injected fetch over the pinned archive fixtures, covers: - progress lines during ranking - an interrupted run (the fetch raises after N files) that resumes on rerun without refetching written months - --restart - a checksum-mismatch month that is skipped and reported, with exit 1 - an unexpected error giving one stderr line and no traceback No network, and it passes under pytest-xdist.
bug.actual: Root cause: bars_backfill computes the whole ranking and fetch in memory before writing, prints nothing until symbols are written, and lets exceptions escape main().
bug.constraints: The output layout and universe.json fields are unchanged No file outside the two listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
